actual_assessment_verbatim.choice: Frozen blinded assessment: Q is my working choice, with P preserved as a serious alternative in a note. This is a modest contextual preference; the pregnancy’s temporal location remains genuinely disputable. R is the least suitable English rendering.
actual_assessment_verbatim.P: Defensible prospective interpretation. It turns the pregnancy adjective into a future transition into pregnancy, so the conception event and its future placement are interpretive decisions, not explicit tense information in הָרָה. The promised sign and announcement parallels support that decision. Natural English; requires a note acknowledging an already pregnant woman.
actual_assessment_verbatim.Q: Best working balance. It retains pregnancy as a state and expresses birth as the subsequent event expected in this announcement. “Is” nevertheless selects present pregnancy where Hebrew supplies no tensed copula. Natural English; requires a note acknowledging prospective pregnancy/conception.
actual_assessment_verbatim.R: Reflects the source’s adjective-plus-participle appearance, but English present progressive does not preserve Hebrew temporal openness. In this sentence, “is bearing a son” can suggest delivery underway; a broader pregnancy sense is possible but awkward after “is pregnant.” The contextual controls do not establish labor underway. Its apparent formal consistency therefore carries a greater risk of misleading readers.
actual_assessment_verbatim.present_countercase: The strongest present-pregnancy case is the state adjective הָרָה, the demonstrative presentation with הִנֵּה, and the definite woman, which together can present a recognizable woman’s existing condition. The child’s development then supplies the deadline in 7:16. Genesis 16:11 supports that state-plus-subsequent-birth reading because 16:4 independently narrates conception. However, Isaiah supplies no equivalent preceding conception narrative in the inspected context. Definiteness and “behold” make the present interpretation plausible without establishing that the woman was physically indicated or visibly pregnant.
actual_assessment_verbatim.prospective_countercase: The strongest prospective case is the surrounding promise of a sign and announcement of the child’s future circumstances. Judges 13:2–3 establishes barrenness and prospectively announces conception and birth; 13:5 and 13:7 then use the pregnancy-plus-bearing formula. That supplies a substantial control against treating such a formula as necessarily present pregnancy. The Isaiah deadline can also operate with forthcoming conception followed by birth. It does not independently decide between P and Q.
actual_assessment_verbatim.conclusion: Genesis and Judges therefore constrain opposite overclaims: Genesis prevents excluding present pregnancy, while Judges prevents making it obligatory. Consistency should follow contextual timing rather than impose identical English tense on related Hebrew formulas.
actual_assessment_verbatim.required_note: Or, “the young woman will conceive and bear a son.” The Hebrew describes pregnancy and bearing without an explicit tense marker; the announcement can also be understood prospectively.
actual_assessment_verbatim.grammar_observation: GKC explicitly illustrates present pregnancy with Genesis 16:11 and includes Isaiah 7:14 among future/imminent participial announcements. That latter classification strengthens the prospective case but does not turn the pregnancy adjective into an explicitly future conception verb.
actual_assessment_verbatim.inspection: Inspected evidence: only source.text from Isaiah 7:10–13,15–17; Genesis 16:1–12; Judges 13:1–7, extracted with Ruby YAML, plus the specified GKC sections in Wikisource transcription. I did not inspect Isaiah 7:14’s repository file, candidate mappings, translation history, research reports, or commercial English translations. The Swete future-Greek control was supplied by the parent and was not independently inspected; it supports an ancient prospective interpretation without uniquely determining Hebrew timing. No edits were made.

root_reason: Accept the narrow birth-English improvement and qualify the pregnancy interpretation; this assessment diagnoses rendering, not ancient wording.
